newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end higher after flat trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end higher after flat trade.

text.p: Singapore shares climbed moments before Tuesday's close to end up on a flat day when buyers kept a wary eye on Wall Street, traders said.
"We're still quite cheery in the market, but the momentum has dropped off a bit," one dealer at a local firm said.
"Monday's rise was on the back of U.S. bouyancy. Buyers are taking a breather in case Wall Street corrects," said another.
A last minute jump from Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) component stocks saw the STII end up 11.49 at 2,112.97.
Total market volume was a moderate 154.5 million units producing 129 gainers against 253 losers.
Gainers were led by City Developments warrants, up Singapore $0.30 at S$10.70, while losers were topped by Creative Technology, down S$2.10 at S$26.90 on profit taking.
Singapore Telecom was among the most actively traded shares, with 9.1 million units moving.
The stock end up S$0.08 at S$2.69, little changed by news that mobile communications rival MobileOne had slashed pager rates to undercut SingTel's hefty reduction in April.
Top active was Elec & Eltek which saw 14 million shares placed out to international investors by its Hong Kong parent.
